content.introduction: According to FactSet, the estimated year-over-year earnings growth rate for Q3 2026 is 29.5%, which is above the 5-year average of 13.3% and the 10-year average of 12.6%. This marks the third consecutive quarter of earnings growth above 25% and the eighth consecutive quarter of double-digit earnings growth for the S&P 500 index. The earnings season is expected to begin in earnest during the second full week of October. Despite unresolved issues like the Iran war and rising government borrowing costs, the American consumer's resilience is expected to support company earnings this quarter.
body:
US financial data group FactSet forecasts earnings for the S&P 500 index grew by 29.1% in Q3 2026, which will mark the third-straight quarter of earnings growth above 25% for the index.

The calendar below, which we will update every week, shows the US companies most held and actively traded by interactive investor customers that are about to report results in the next two weeks.

Image 14: combination of US company logos

## Upcoming earnings [...] Third-quarter earnings season is due to begin in earnest during the second full week of October. Many of the issues dictating market direction for much of 2026 remain unresolved, principally the Iran war whose impact on inflation is affecting central bank policy worldwide. You can add rising government borrowing costs, tariffs and AI bubble fears to the mix. Despite this, the American consumer remains resilient which is expected to bode well for company earnings this quarter. # US earnings season - Q3 2026

Earnings season in the United States is a period where a large number of publicly-traded US companies report their quarterly earnings.

See upcoming earningsInvest with ii

The estimated (year-over-year) earnings growth rate for Q3 2026 is 29.5%, which is above the 5-year average earnings growth rate of 13.3% and above the 10-year average earnings growth rate of 12.6%. If 29.5% is the actual growth rate for the quarter, it will mark the 3 rd consecutive quarter of year-over-year earnings growth above 25% and the 8 th consecutive quarter of double-digit earnings growth for the index. [...] During the past week, the estimated earnings growth rate for the S&P 500 for Q3 2026 increased to 29.5% from 29.2%. The positive EPS surprise reported by Micron Technology ($33.42 vs $31.77) was the largest contributor to the increase in the overall earnings growth rate for the index during the week. [...] • Earnings Revisions: On June 30, the estimated (year-over-year) earnings growth rate for the S&P 500 for Q3 2026 was 26.7%. Four sectors are expected to report higher earnings today (compared to June 30) due to upward revisions to EPS estimates. 

• Earnings Guidance: For Q3 2026, 44 S&P 500 companies have issued negative EPS guidance and 72 S&P 500 companies have issued positive EPS guidance.

Due to the upward revisions to earnings estimates by analysts and the positive EPS guidance issued by companies, the estimated (year-over-year) earnings growth rate for Q3 2026 is higher today relative to the start of the third quarter. As of today, the S&P 500 is expected to report (year-over-year) earnings growth of 29.5%, compared to the estimated (year-over-year) earnings growth rate of 26.7% on June 30. [...] If 29.5% is the actual growth rate for the quarter, it will mark the third consecutive quarter of earnings growth above 25% and the eighth consecutive quarter of double-digit earnings growth for the index.

All eleven sectors are projected to report year-over-year growth. Five of these eleven sectors are predicted to report double-digit growth, led by the Energy, Information Technology, Communication Services, and Materials sectors. [...] S&P 500 companies issuing positive EPS guidance for Q3 2026 is 62% (72 out of 116), which is also well above the 5-year average of 40% and well above the 10-year average of 41%.
